video.title: Everyone Chases Trends. Resell This Instead to Actually Make Money

summary: Chris Koerner hosts liquidation expert Shannon, who screens liquidation and government auction sites (Costco/Target liquidation auctions, GovDeals, GSA Auctions) and walks through example lots: plumbing fixtures, train sets, pool floats, furniture, patio furniture, Tesla superchargers, a Blackhawk simulator, electric buses, aircraft and lighthouses. The core playbook is to buy boring, seasonal goods, work backwards from a verified resale price, test demand on Facebook Marketplace before bidding, and scale from pallets to truckloads. Member success stories (pressure washers, patio furniture) are cited as proof. Shannon sells a mastermind and Chris sells a community, so evidence is mostly second-hand and promotional.

ideas.name: Pallet and truckload liquidation reselling via Facebook Marketplace
ideas.one_liner: Buy overstock and customer-return pallets from retailer liquidation auctions cheaply and resell locally via Facebook Marketplace and eBay.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales; margin between auction price plus freight and resale price
ideas.customer: Local consumers on Facebook Marketplace, plus flippers, remodelers and contractors
ideas.problem: Retailers must move huge volumes of returns and overstock quickly, so goods sell far below retail
ideas.offer: Brand-new or lightly used branded goods at roughly half retail or less

pricing.model: Resale at about 50% of retail or below, based on researched sold prices

price_points.label: Hearth & Hand wooden train set near Christmas

pricing.notes: Rule: 'retail price is a lie', cut MSRP in half and verify with sold listings

acquisition_channels.details: List on Facebook Marketplace (even before bidding to test demand), sell on eBay, live-sell; post in Facebook groups; garage/driveway sales

quote.text: Started posting in Facebook groups. Do we have this? The phone started ringing. They had a $2,000 day on Labor Day selling stuff out of their driveway.
quote.speaker: Shannon

acquisition_channels.details: Capture customer emails and ask what else they buy; email them when new shipments land; share manifests with network contacts to price lots

ideas.delivery: Owner personally sources via auction, arranges freight (freight forwarder breaks truckloads into smaller pallets for residential delivery), stores in garage, tests and fixes items, and hands over locally; physical handling needs helpers
unit_economics_claims: Train set lot of 240 units sold for $2,600 (about $11 each) vs Target retail $130
Costco furniture truckload retail $11,440 sold for $585
Walker Edison outdoor truckload of 250 units sold for $7,240, about $10k with freight
Sacramento member sold 600 pressure washers in 10 months
Member recouped truckload cost in 36 hours and hit $17,000 record month
ideas.startup_cost: Small: a pallet can be ~$750; truckload about $7k-10k including freight
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Weeks (about 2-3 weeks to receive goods); one member profitable within 72 hours of receiving a truckload

acquisition.how: Marketplace listings can be drafted and posted with AI tooling, but local buyer chat and pickup coordination need a human.

onboarding.how: Auction bidding and price research can be tool-assisted; freight booking and checking lots need human judgment.

delivery.how: Moving, storing, testing, repairing and handing over heavy physical goods is manual.

billing.how: Mostly cash or app payments on pickup; online sales are payment-platform handled but still need a person.

support.how: Buyer questions and disputes can be partly automated; returns and defects need a human.

uk_applicability.notes: UK has equivalents (B-Stock, Amazon/Argos/John Lewis liquidation pallets, Gumtree, eBay, Facebook Marketplace) but Costco/Target US auction access and prices differ. Distribution is local and heavy goods need storage. Consumer-law obligations on sold goods apply (Consumer Rights Act, product safety, WEEE for electricals).

risks: Resale value uncertain if you skip price research
Heavy goods need storage, helpers and freight
Seasonal inventory may sit for months
Damaged or broken items such as pressure washers need repair

tactics.name: Work backwards from sale price
steps: Research sold listings on eBay and Marketplace
Halve MSRP as a conservative estimate
Share manifests with trade contacts for real values
Only bid after you know your exit price

quote.text: You should know exactly what you're going to sell this product for before you place any bids
quote.speaker: Shannon

tactics.name: Test demand before bidding
steps: List the item on Facebook Marketplace before winning
Include the expiry date or condition and watch reactions

tactics.name: Buy boring and seasonal
steps: Target boring listings with poor titles
Buy seasonal goods off-season or just before peak
Scale to truckloads to eliminate beginner competition

warnings.warning: Never trust MSRP; research real market price

quote.text: don't fall for this this MSRP. You have to research the market price because that's all that matters.
quote.speaker: Shannon

warnings.warning: Avoid expensive shipping from far away; buy closer to home
Beginners should not buy lots they don't know how to sell
Winning bidders sometimes fail to pay, which re-lists lots

lessons.lesson: Boring products face less competition than shiny ones.

quote.text: everybody's fighting for the sexy stuff and you should leave that stuff alone and focus on boring stuff
quote.speaker: Shannon

lessons.lesson: A weak or lazy listing title is a signal that few bidders will compete.
Buying truckloads removes most beginner competition and creates a moat.
Treat freight as part of cost of goods and judge on total margin.
Seasonal stock reduces the risk of hidden defects because overstock is a forecasting error.
Run a hobby flip like a business by capturing customer data.
Show up daily to browse auctions to develop pattern recognition.
Ask the auction seller questions; there are many reasons to skip, but opportunity is missed.

evidence_quality.rationale: Mostly second-hand member anecdotes and auction-lot walk-throughs with unverified resale values; Shannon has genuine experience but gives few first-hand figures. Many items are hypotheticals or fun ideas.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Shannon sells a mastermind; Chris sells TK Owners community and reads a GoHighLevel sponsor ad.
